jail-incarceration.context: Incarceration takes a toll on individuals, families and communities. Black and Latino New Yorkers experience higher policing compared with non-Latino white New Yorkers. This leads to higher rates of detention, which may include long periods of time spent in jail before trial. People who have been incarcerated are more likely to experience mental and physical health problems. They may also have trouble finding employment and housing and accessing healthy food.

heat-vulnerability-index.context: The risk of death from heat is inequitably distributed across neighborhoods. Each neighborhood's environmental and social factors are used to create a heat vulnerability index (HVI), with values ranging from 1 to 5 for each community district, where 5 represents the highest heat vulnerability and 1 represents the lowest.
heat-vulnerability-index.comparison: In CD <NAME> the heat vulnerability is <Value> out of 5.
heat-vulnerability-index.indicatorDetail: The Heat Vulnerability Index is made from data on surface temperature, green space, air conditioning access, median income, and Black population (the population most excluded from heat resources). Differences in community-level heat impacts stem from structural racism, which limits access to preventive resources.
